ch_gram_b2_01.title: Past Subjunctive
ch_gram_b2_01.theory:
## Past Subjunctive (-ra / -se forms)

The **past subjunctive** (also called the imperfect subjunctive) is one of the most important verb forms at the B2 level. It is used to express wishes, hypothetical situations, polite requests, and actions in the past that require the subjunctive mood.

### Formation

The past subjunctive is formed from the **third person plural (ellos) of the preterite**. Drop the **-ron** ending and add the past subjunctive endings.

| Preterite (ellos) | Stem | -ra form | -se form |
|---|---|---|---|
| habla**ron** | habla- | hablara | hablase |
| comie**ron** | comie- | comiera | comiese |
| vivie**ron** | vivie- | viviera | viviese |

### Full Conjugation: hablar
| Person | -ra form | -se form |
|---|---|---|
| yo | hablara | hablase |
| tú | hablaras | hablases |
| él/ella/usted | hablara | hablase |
| nosotros | habláramos | hablásemos |
| vosotros | hablarais | hablaseis |
| ellos/ustedes | hablaran | hablasen |

### Irregular Stems (from preterite)
| Infinitive | Preterite (ellos) | Past Subj. Stem |
|---|---|---|
| ser/ir | fueron | fue- → fuera/fuese |
| tener | tuvieron | tuvie- → tuviera/tuviese |
| hacer | hicieron | hicie- → hiciera/hiciese |
| poder | pudieron | pudie- → pudiera/pudiese |
| poner | pusieron | pusie- → pusiera/pusiese |
| querer | quisieron | quisie- → quisiera/quisiese |
| saber | supieron | supie- → supiera/supiese |
| decir | dijeron | dije- → dijera/dijese |
| traer | trajeron | traje- → trajera/trajese |

### Key Uses
1. **After 'si' (if) in hypothetical conditions**: Si tuviera dinero, viajaría. (If I had money, I would travel.)
2. **Wishes with 'ojalá'**: Ojalá pudiera ir contigo. (I wish I could go with you.)
3. **Polite requests**: Quisiera un café. (I would like a coffee.)
4. **Past actions requiring subjunctive**: Me pidió que hablara más despacio. (He asked me to speak more slowly.)
5. **After 'como si' (as if)**: Habla como si fuera español. (He speaks as if he were Spanish.)

### -ra vs -se: Are They Interchangeable?
Both forms are grammatically interchangeable in most cases. However, the **-ra form** is far more common in everyday speech, especially in Latin America. The **-se form** is considered more literary or formal and is more common in Spain.
key_points: Formed from the 3rd person plural preterite: drop -ron, add -ra/-se endings
The -ra form is more common in speech; -se is more literary
Used after 'si' (if) for hypothetical conditions, with 'ojalá', and after 'como si'
All irregular preterite stems carry over: tuvieron → tuviera, pudieron → pudiera
Nosotros forms carry a written accent: habláramos, comiéramos

vocab_list.example_meaning: I would like a coffee, please.

vocab_list.example_meaning: I wish I could fly.

vocab_list.example: Si fuera rico, compraría una isla.

ch_gram_b2_02.title: Conditional Type 2
ch_gram_b2_02.theory:
## Conditional Type 2 — Hypothetical Present/Future

Conditional Type 2 sentences express **hypothetical or unlikely situations** in the present or future. They describe what **would happen** if something **were** the case (but it isn't).

### Structure

**Si + past subjunctive, conditional simple**

| Si clause (condition) | Main clause (result) |
|---|---|
| Si + imperfect subjunctive | conditional simple |
| Si tuviera tiempo... | ...iría al cine. |

### Conditional Simple Conjugation
Formed with the full infinitive + endings (-ía, -ías, -ía, -íamos, -íais, -ían).

| Person | hablar | comer | vivir |
|---|---|---|---|
| yo | hablaría | comería | viviría |
| tú | hablarías | comerías | vivirías |
| él/ella | hablaría | comería | viviría |
| nosotros | hablaríamos | comeríamos | viviríamos |
| vosotros | hablaríais | comeríais | viviríais |
| ellos | hablarían | comerían | vivirían |

### Irregular Conditional Stems
| Infinitive | Stem | Example |
|---|---|---|
| tener | tendr- | tendría |
| poder | podr- | podría |
| salir | saldr- | saldría |
| hacer | har- | haría |
| decir | dir- | diría |
| querer | querr- | querría |
| saber | sabr- | sabría |
| haber | habr- | habría |
| venir | vendr- | vendría |
| poner | pondr- | pondría |

### Examples
- **Si tuviera más tiempo, estudiaría español.** — If I had more time, I would study Spanish.
- **Si viviera en España, comería paella todos los días.** — If I lived in Spain, I would eat paella every day.
- **Si pudiera elegir, trabajaría desde casa.** — If I could choose, I would work from home.

### Common Pitfalls
- **Never use the conditional in the si-clause**: ~~Si tendría~~ → Si tuviera
- **Never use the present subjunctive in Type 2**: ~~Si tenga~~ → Si tuviera
- The clause order can be reversed: **Viajaría más si tuviera dinero.**

### Type 1 vs Type 2
| Type | Structure | Likelihood |
|---|---|---|
| Type 1 | Si + present indicative, future | Possible/likely |
| Type 2 | Si + past subjunctive, conditional | Unlikely/hypothetical |
key_points: Structure: Si + past subjunctive, conditional simple
Never use the conditional tense in the si-clause (Si tuviera, NOT Si tendría)
Irregular conditional stems are the same as irregular future stems (tendr-, podr-, har-)
Used for hypothetical or unlikely situations in the present/future
Clause order is flexible: the si-clause can come first or second

vocab_list.example: Si no lloviera, habría más gente en el parque.
vocab_list.example_meaning: If it weren't raining, there would be more people in the park.

ch_gram_b2_03.title: Conditional Type 3
ch_gram_b2_03.theory:
## Conditional Type 3 — Unreal Past

Conditional Type 3 sentences describe **hypothetical situations in the past** — things that did **not** happen. They express regret, missed opportunities, or alternative outcomes.

### Structure

**Si + pluperfect subjunctive, conditional perfect**

| Si clause (condition) | Main clause (result) |
|---|---|
| Si + hubiera/hubiese + past participle | conditional perfect (habría + past participle) |
| Si hubiera estudiado... | ...habría aprobado. |

### Pluperfect Subjunctive Formation
hubiera/hubiese + past participle

| Person | Form |
|---|---|
| yo | hubiera/hubiese hablado |
| tú | hubieras/hubieses hablado |
| él/ella | hubiera/hubiese hablado |
| nosotros | hubiéramos/hubiésemos hablado |
| vosotros | hubierais/hubieseis hablado |
| ellos | hubieran/hubiesen hablado |

### Conditional Perfect Formation
habría + past participle

| Person | Form |
|---|---|
| yo | habría hablado |
| tú | habrías hablado |
| él/ella | habría hablado |
| nosotros | habríamos hablado |
| vosotros | habríais hablado |
| ellos | habrían hablado |

### Examples
- **Si hubiera estudiado más, habría aprobado el examen.** — If I had studied more, I would have passed the exam.
- **Si hubiéramos salido antes, habríamos llegado a tiempo.** — If we had left earlier, we would have arrived on time.
- **Si no hubiera llovido, habríamos ido a la playa.** — If it hadn't rained, we would have gone to the beach.

### Colloquial Variation
In colloquial Spanish, the pluperfect subjunctive can replace the conditional perfect in the result clause:
- **Si hubiera sabido, hubiera venido.** (instead of *habría venido*)
This is widely used in speech but considered less formal in writing.

### Common Pitfalls
- Do not confuse Type 2 (present hypothetical) with Type 3 (past hypothetical)
- The past participle never changes form — it always ends in -ado/-ido
- Irregular past participles remain the same: hecho, dicho, escrito, visto, puesto, vuelto, abierto, roto
key_points: Structure: Si + pluperfect subjunctive, conditional perfect
Describes hypothetical past events that did NOT happen
Pluperfect subjunctive: hubiera/hubiese + past participle
Conditional perfect: habría + past participle
Colloquially, hubiera can replace habría in the result clause

vocab_list.example: Si lo hubiera sabido, no habría venido.
vocab_list.example_meaning: If I had known, I wouldn't have come.

vocab_list.example: Habría llamado, pero no tenía tu número.
vocab_list.example_meaning: I would have called, but I didn't have your number.

vocab_list.example: Si hubiera estudiado, habría aprobado.
vocab_list.example_meaning: If I had studied, I would have passed.

vocab_list.example: Si hubiéramos corrido, habríamos llegado a tiempo.
vocab_list.example_meaning: If we had run, we would have arrived on time.

ch_gram_b2_04.title: Conditional Perfect
ch_gram_b2_04.theory:
## The Conditional Perfect (Condicional Compuesto)

The conditional perfect expresses what **would have happened** under certain conditions. It is also used to express **probability or conjecture about a past action** viewed from another past moment.

### Formation

**habría + past participle**

| Person | Example (hablar) |
|---|---|
| yo | habría hablado |
| tú | habrías hablado |
| él/ella/usted | habría hablado |
| nosotros | habríamos hablado |
| vosotros | habríais hablado |
| ellos/ustedes | habrían hablado |

### Irregular Past Participles
| Infinitive | Past Participle |
|---|---|
| hacer | hecho |
| decir | dicho |
| escribir | escrito |
| ver | visto |
| poner | puesto |
| volver | vuelto |
| abrir | abierto |
| romper | roto |
| morir | muerto |
| cubrir | cubierto |

### Key Uses

1. **Hypothetical past result (Type 3 conditional)**:
   - Si hubiera tenido tiempo, **habría viajado** a Japón. — If I had had time, I would have traveled to Japan.

2. **Past probability / conjecture**:
   - A las diez ya **habrían llegado**. — By ten they would have (probably) already arrived.
   - **Habrían sido** las tres cuando llamó. — It must have been around three when he called.

3. **Expressing regret or unfulfilled wishes**:
   - **Habría preferido** quedarme en casa. — I would have preferred to stay at home.
   - Yo no **habría hecho** eso. — I would not have done that.

4. **Reported speech (future perfect → conditional perfect)**:
   - Direct: "Para junio habré terminado." → Reported: Dijo que para junio **habría terminado**.

### Conditional Perfect vs Pluperfect Subjunctive
In spoken Spanish, the pluperfect subjunctive (-ra form) sometimes replaces the conditional perfect:
- **Habría ido** / **Hubiera ido** — both mean "I would have gone."
key_points: Formation: habría + past participle (hablado, comido, vivido)
Used in the result clause of Type 3 conditionals (Si hubiera..., habría...)
Expresses past probability: 'Habrían sido las tres' = It must have been three
Irregular participles: hecho, dicho, escrito, visto, puesto, vuelto
In speech, hubiera + participle can substitute habría + participle

vocab_list.example: Yo no habría dicho eso en público.
vocab_list.example_meaning: I would not have said that in public.

vocab_list.example: ¿Qué habrías hecho en mi lugar?
vocab_list.example_meaning: What would you have done in my place?

vocab_list.example_meaning: I would have gone with you, but I was sick.

ch_gram_b2_05.title: Future Perfect
ch_gram_b2_05.theory:
## The Future Perfect (Futuro Compuesto / Futuro Perfecto)

The future perfect expresses an action that **will have been completed** by a certain point in the future. It is also widely used to express **conjecture or probability about past events**.

### Formation

**habré + past participle**

| Person | Example (terminar) |
|---|---|
| yo | habré terminado |
| tú | habrás terminado |
| él/ella/usted | habrá terminado |
| nosotros | habremos terminado |
| vosotros | habréis terminado |
| ellos/ustedes | habrán terminado |

### Key Uses

1. **Action completed before a future point**:
   - Para las cinco, **habré terminado** el informe. — By five, I will have finished the report.
   - Cuando llegues, ya **habremos comido**. — When you arrive, we will have already eaten.

2. **Conjecture / probability about the recent past**:
   - ¿Dónde estará Juan? **Habrá salido** del trabajo. — Where is Juan? He has probably left work.
   - **Habrán llegado** ya, ¿no? — They've probably arrived by now, right?
   - ¿Quién **habrá llamado** a estas horas? — Who could have called at this hour?

3. **Expressing surprise or disbelief about a past action**:
   - ¡No **habrás olvidado** las llaves otra vez! — Don't tell me you've forgotten the keys again!

### Time Markers Often Used
- **para** + time expression: para las ocho, para mañana, para el viernes
- **cuando** + present subjunctive: cuando llegues, cuando termines
- **antes de que** + present subjunctive: antes de que empiece la reunión
- **ya**: Ya habrán comido.

### Future Perfect vs Present Perfect
| Tense | Use | Example |
|---|---|---|
| Present Perfect | Completed in the past with present relevance | He terminado el informe. |
| Future Perfect | Will be completed by a future point OR probability | Habré terminado para las cinco. / Habrá salido. |
key_points: Formation: habré/habrás/habrá/habremos/habréis/habrán + past participle
Expresses actions that will be completed by a future point in time
Widely used to express conjecture about recent past events
Common time markers: para + time, cuando + subj., antes de que + subj.
Do not confuse with conditional perfect (habría) which refers to hypothetical situations

vocab_list.example: Para junio habré terminado la carrera.
vocab_list.example_meaning: By June I will have finished my degree.

vocab_list.meaning: he/she will have left (or probably left)
vocab_list.example: No contesta. Habrá salido de casa.
vocab_list.example_meaning: He's not answering. He's probably left the house.

vocab_list.example: A estas horas ya habrán llegado al hotel.
vocab_list.example_meaning: By now they will have already arrived at the hotel.

ch_gram_b2_06.title: Pluperfect Subjunctive
ch_gram_b2_06.theory:
## The Pluperfect Subjunctive (Pretérito Pluscuamperfecto de Subjuntivo)

The pluperfect subjunctive describes **hypothetical or unreal actions in the past**. It is the past-tense equivalent of the present perfect subjunctive and is essential for Type 3 conditional sentences.

### Formation

**hubiera/hubiese + past participle**

| Person | -ra form | -se form |
|---|---|---|
| yo | hubiera hablado | hubiese hablado |
| tú | hubieras hablado | hubieses hablado |
| él/ella/usted | hubiera hablado | hubiese hablado |
| nosotros | hubiéramos hablado | hubiésemos hablado |
| vosotros | hubierais hablado | hubieseis hablado |
| ellos/ustedes | hubieran hablado | hubiesen hablado |

### Key Uses

1. **Type 3 conditional (si-clause)**:
   - **Si hubiera estudiado**, habría aprobado. — If I had studied, I would have passed.

2. **After 'ojalá' (unfulfilled past wish)**:
   - **Ojalá hubiera ido** a la fiesta. — I wish I had gone to the party.

3. **After 'como si' (past reference)**:
   - Hablaba **como si hubiera vivido** allí toda la vida. — He spoke as if he had lived there his whole life.

4. **After verbs/expressions requiring subjunctive (past context)**:
   - No creía que **hubieran terminado** tan rápido. — I didn't believe they had finished so quickly.
   - Me sorprendió que no **hubiera llamado**. — It surprised me that he hadn't called.

5. **After temporal conjunctions in past context**:
   - Esperé hasta que **hubieran salido** todos. — I waited until everyone had left.

### Pluperfect Subjunctive vs Past Subjunctive
| Tense | Refers to | Example |
|---|---|---|
| Past subjunctive | Simultaneous or future to the main verb | Quería que **viniera**. |
| Pluperfect subjunctive | Prior to the main verb | Dudaba que **hubiera venido**. |

### Common Pitfall
Do not confuse **hubiera** (pluperfect subjunctive of haber) with **hubiera** used colloquially as an alternative to **habría** (conditional perfect). Context determines the meaning.
key_points: Formation: hubiera/hubiese + past participle
Essential for Type 3 conditionals: Si hubiera..., habría...
Used with ojalá for unfulfilled past wishes: Ojalá hubiera ido
Used after como si with a past reference point
Expresses actions prior to another past action in subjunctive contexts

vocab_list.example: Si lo hubiera sabido antes, te habría avisado.
vocab_list.example_meaning: If I had known earlier, I would have warned you.

vocab_list.example: Ojalá hubiera venido a la boda.
vocab_list.example_meaning: I wish he had come to the wedding.

vocab_list.example: No pensé que hubieran terminado tan pronto.

ch_gram_b2_07.title: Concessive Clauses
ch_gram_b2_07.theory:
## Concessive Clauses (Oraciones Concesivas)

Concessive clauses express a **contrast or obstacle** that does not prevent the main action from happening. In English, they correspond to "although," "even though," "despite," etc.

### Key Concessive Connectors

| Connector | Meaning | Mood Required |
|---|---|---|
| **aunque** | although / even though / even if | Indicative or Subjunctive |
| **a pesar de que** | despite the fact that | Indicative or Subjunctive |
| **por más que** | no matter how much | Subjunctive |
| **por mucho que** | no matter how much | Subjunctive |
| **si bien** | although / while | Indicative |
| **aun cuando** | even when / even if | Indicative or Subjunctive |

### Aunque: Indicative vs Subjunctive

The choice of mood after **aunque** changes the meaning:

| Mood | Meaning | Example |
|---|---|---|
| **Indicative** | States a fact | Aunque **llueve**, salimos. (Although it IS raining, we're going out.) |
| **Subjunctive** | Hypothetical or unknown | Aunque **llueva**, saldremos. (Even if it rains, we'll go out.) |

### Detailed Examples

1. **Aunque + indicative (known fact)**:
   - Aunque **está** cansado, sigue trabajando. — Although he IS tired, he keeps working.

2. **Aunque + subjunctive (hypothetical)**:
   - Aunque **esté** cansado, seguirá trabajando. — Even if he IS tired (we don't know), he will keep working.

3. **A pesar de que**:
   - A pesar de que **estudiamos** mucho, no aprobamos. — Despite the fact that we studied a lot, we didn't pass.

4. **Por más que / Por mucho que** (always subjunctive):
   - Por más que **intente**, no lo consigue. — No matter how much he tries, he can't do it.
   - Por mucho que **estudies**, este examen es difícil. — No matter how much you study, this exam is hard.

5. **Si bien** (formal, always indicative):
   - Si bien **es** caro, la calidad es excelente. — Although it is expensive, the quality is excellent.

### A pesar de + infinitive / noun
When the subject is the same in both clauses, use **a pesar de + infinitive**:
- A pesar de **estar** cansado, fue al gimnasio. — Despite being tired, he went to the gym.

With a noun:
- A pesar de **la lluvia**, fuimos a la playa. — Despite the rain, we went to the beach.
key_points: Aunque + indicative = known fact; aunque + subjunctive = hypothetical
Por más que / por mucho que always take the subjunctive
Si bien is formal and always takes the indicative
A pesar de + infinitive when both clauses share the same subject
Concessive clauses express an obstacle that does not prevent the main action

vocab_list.example: Aunque llueva, iremos al parque.
vocab_list.example_meaning: Even if it rains, we will go to the park.

vocab_list.example: A pesar de que es difícil, no me rindo.
vocab_list.example_meaning: Despite the fact that it's hard, I don't give up.

vocab_list.example: Por más que lo intento, no puedo entenderlo.
vocab_list.example_meaning: No matter how much I try, I can't understand it.

vocab_list.example: Si bien es joven, tiene mucha experiencia.
vocab_list.example_meaning: Although he is young, he has a lot of experience.

ch_gram_b2_08.title: Advanced Relative Clauses
ch_gram_b2_08.theory:
## Advanced Relative Clauses

At the B2 level, you need to go beyond basic **que** and master a range of relative pronouns and the distinction between restrictive and non-restrictive clauses.

### Relative Pronouns Overview

| Pronoun | Use | Example |
|---|---|---|
| **que** | Most common, for people and things | El libro **que** leí... |
| **quien(es)** | For people (after prepositions, non-restrictive) | La persona **con quien** hablé... |
| **el/la/los/las que** | After prepositions, for specificity | La casa **en la que** vivo... |
| **el/la cual, los/las cuales** | Formal, after prepositions (especially long ones) | El problema **sobre el cual** hablamos... |
| **lo que** | Refers to an idea/concept (neuter) | No entiendo **lo que** dices. |
| **lo cual** | Refers back to a whole clause (neuter) | Llegó tarde, **lo cual** me molestó. |
| **cuyo/a/os/as** | Possessive relative (whose) | El autor **cuyo** libro leí... |
| **donde** | Relative adverb of place | La ciudad **donde** nací... |

### Restrictive vs Non-Restrictive Clauses

**Restrictive** (defining): essential information, no commas.
- Los estudiantes **que aprobaron** pueden irse. — The students who passed can leave. (Only those who passed.)

**Non-restrictive** (explanatory): extra information, with commas.
- Los estudiantes, **que aprobaron**, pueden irse. — The students, who passed, can leave. (All of them passed.)

### Cuyo/a/os/as (Whose)
**Cuyo** agrees with the **noun it modifies** (not the antecedent):
- El escritor **cuya** novela ganó el premio... — The writer whose novel won the prize...
- Los países **cuyos** gobiernos firmaron... — The countries whose governments signed...

### After Prepositions
When a preposition is needed, use **el/la/los/las que** or **el/la cual**:
- La empresa **para la que** trabajo es grande. — The company I work for is big.
- El tema **sobre el cual** investigamos... — The topic we researched...

### Lo que vs Lo cual
- **Lo que** introduces a new idea: **Lo que** me gusta es la música. (What I like is music.)
- **Lo cual** refers back to a previous clause: No vino, **lo cual** me sorprendió. (He didn't come, which surprised me.)

### Common Pitfall: Que vs Quien After Prepositions
- Use **quien** (not que) for people after prepositions: La persona **con quien** hablé (NOT ~~con que~~).
- Alternatively: La persona **con la que** hablé (also correct).
key_points: Cuyo/a/os/as means 'whose' and agrees with the following noun, not the antecedent
Lo que introduces new ideas; lo cual refers back to a previous clause
After prepositions, use el/la/los/las que or quien(es) for people
Non-restrictive clauses use commas and add extra (non-essential) information
El/la cual forms are preferred in formal writing and after longer prepositions

vocab_list.example: El profesor cuyo curso tomé es muy bueno.
vocab_list.example_meaning: The professor whose course I took is very good.

vocab_list.example: Aprobé el examen, lo cual me alegró mucho.
vocab_list.example_meaning: I passed the exam, which made me very happy.

vocab_list.example: No entiendo lo que estás diciendo.
vocab_list.example_meaning: I don't understand what you're saying.

vocab_list.example: La chica con quien salgo es de Sevilla.
vocab_list.example_meaning: The girl I'm going out with is from Seville.

ch_gram_b2_09.title: Nominalization
ch_gram_b2_09.theory:
## Nominalization (La Nominalización)

Nominalization is the process of **turning adjectives, verbs, or clauses into nouns** by using articles or other determiners. It allows you to avoid repetition and express ideas more concisely.

### Nominalization with Articles

Instead of repeating a noun, use the definite article alone:
- Quiero **el** rojo. — I want the red one. (instead of "el coche rojo")
- Prefiero **las** grandes. — I prefer the big ones.
- Dame **los** de arriba. — Give me the ones from above.

### Neuter Article 'Lo'

**Lo** + adjective creates abstract nouns:
| Expression | Meaning |
|---|---|
| **lo bueno** | the good thing / what's good |
| **lo malo** | the bad thing |
| **lo interesante** | the interesting thing |
| **lo importante** | the important thing |
| **lo difícil** | the difficult thing |
| **lo mejor** | the best thing |
| **lo peor** | the worst thing |

**Examples:**
- **Lo mejor** de la película es el final. — The best thing about the movie is the ending.
- **Lo difícil** es empezar. — The hard part is starting.
- No sabes **lo cansado** que estoy. — You don't know how tired I am.

### Lo + adjective/adverb + que (exclamatory intensity)
This construction expresses degree or intensity:
- No imaginas **lo lejos que** está. — You can't imagine how far it is.
- Ya verás **lo rápido que** aprende. — You'll see how quickly he learns.

### Nominalization with 'el que / la que / los que / las que'
These replace a noun previously mentioned:
- De todos los restaurantes, **el que** más me gusta es este. — Of all the restaurants, the one I like most is this one.
- **Los que** lleguen tarde no podrán entrar. — Those who arrive late won't be able to enter.

### Nominalization with 'lo que'
- **Lo que** necesitas es descansar. — What you need is to rest.
- Haz **lo que** quieras. — Do whatever you want.

### Infinitive as Noun
Infinitives can function as nouns (always masculine):
- **El saber** no ocupa lugar. — Knowledge takes up no space.
- **Comer** bien es importante. — Eating well is important.
key_points: Lo + adjective creates abstract nouns: lo bueno, lo importante, lo mejor
Lo + adjective/adverb + que expresses degree: No sabes lo lejos que está
El/la/los/las + adjective replaces a previously mentioned noun
Los que / las que can mean 'those who' or 'the ones that'
Infinitives function as masculine nouns: El saber, el comer

ch_gram_b2_10.title: Discourse Connectors
ch_gram_b2_10.theory:
## Discourse Connectors (Conectores del Discurso)

Discourse connectors are words and phrases that **link ideas, sentences, and paragraphs** to create coherent and fluent text. Mastering them is essential for B2-level writing and speaking.

### Adding Information
| Connector | Meaning |
|---|---|
| **además** | moreover / besides / in addition |
| **también** | also |
| **asimismo** | likewise / also (formal) |
| **incluso** | even |
| **es más** | what's more |
| **aparte de** | apart from |
| **no solo... sino también** | not only... but also |

### Contrasting Ideas
| Connector | Meaning |
|---|---|
| **sin embargo** | however |
| **no obstante** | nevertheless |
| **en cambio** | on the other hand / instead |
| **por el contrario** | on the contrary |
| **a pesar de (que)** | despite (the fact that) |
| **aunque** | although / even though |
| **mientras que** | while / whereas |

### Cause and Reason
| Connector | Meaning |
|---|---|
| **porque** | because |
| **ya que** | since / given that |
| **puesto que** | since / given that (formal) |
| **dado que** | given that |
| **debido a (que)** | due to (the fact that) |
| **como** | since / as (at beginning of sentence) |

### Consequence and Result
| Connector | Meaning |
|---|---|
| **por eso** | that's why / therefore |
| **por lo tanto** | therefore |
| **así que** | so |
| **de modo que** | so that / in such a way that |
| **en consecuencia** | consequently |
| **de ahí que** + subjunctive | hence / that's why |

### Purpose
| Connector | Meaning |
|---|---|
| **para (que)** | in order to / so that |
| **con el fin de (que)** | with the aim of |
| **a fin de (que)** | in order to |

### Organizing Discourse
| Connector | Meaning |
|---|---|
| **en primer lugar** | in the first place |
| **por un lado... por otro (lado)** | on the one hand... on the other |
| **en cuanto a** | as for / regarding |
| **respecto a** | with respect to |
| **por último** | lastly |
| **en resumen** | in summary |
| **en conclusión** | in conclusion |

### Examples in Context
- **Además**, el precio incluye el desayuno. — Moreover, the price includes breakfast.
- Estudia mucho; **sin embargo**, no aprueba. — He studies a lot; however, he doesn't pass.
- **Ya que** estás aquí, ayúdame. — Since you're here, help me.
- Llovía mucho, **por lo tanto** nos quedamos en casa. — It was raining a lot, therefore we stayed home.
- **En primer lugar**, quiero agradecer a todos. — In the first place, I want to thank everyone.
key_points: Sin embargo / no obstante = however/nevertheless (contrast)
Ya que / puesto que / dado que = since/given that (cause, more formal than porque)
Por lo tanto / en consecuencia = therefore/consequently (result)
De ahí que always requires the subjunctive
En primer lugar, por un lado/por otro, en conclusión help organize discourse

vocab_list.example_meaning: It's expensive; however, it's worth it.

vocab_list.example_meaning: Since you're not coming, I'll go alone.

vocab_list.example_meaning: She's intelligent and, moreover, very hard-working.

ch_gram_b2_11.title: Verbal Periphrasis
ch_gram_b2_11.theory:
## Verbal Periphrasis (Perífrasis Verbales)

A verbal periphrasis is a **combination of two or more verbs** that function as a single unit, where the first verb (auxiliary) is conjugated and the second is in a non-finite form (infinitive, gerund, or participle). They express nuances like obligation, probability, continuity, and phases of an action.

### Periphrasis with Infinitive

| Periphrasis | Meaning | Example |
|---|---|---|
| **ir a** + inf. | to be going to | Voy a estudiar. |
| **tener que** + inf. | to have to (obligation) | Tengo que salir. |
| **hay que** + inf. | one must (impersonal) | Hay que estudiar más. |
| **deber** + inf. | must / should (obligation) | Debes llegar a tiempo. |
| **deber de** + inf. | must (probability) | Debe de estar en casa. |
| **poder** + inf. | to be able to / can | Puedo ayudarte. |
| **soler** + inf. | to usually do | Suelo correr por las mañanas. |
| **volver a** + inf. | to do again | Volvió a llamar. |
| **dejar de** + inf. | to stop doing | Dejó de fumar. |
| **acabar de** + inf. | to have just done | Acabo de llegar. |
| **ponerse a** + inf. | to start (suddenly) | Se puso a llover. |
| **echarse a** + inf. | to burst into | Se echó a llorar. |
| **llegar a** + inf. | to manage to / to end up | Llegó a ser presidente. |

### Periphrasis with Gerund

| Periphrasis | Meaning | Example |
|---|---|---|
| **estar** + gerund | to be doing (progressive) | Estoy estudiando. |
| **seguir / continuar** + gerund | to keep on doing | Sigue lloviendo. |
| **llevar** + time + gerund | to have been doing for | Llevo dos horas esperando. |
| **ir** + gerund | to gradually do | Va mejorando poco a poco. |
| **andar** + gerund | to go around doing | Anda buscando trabajo. |

### Periphrasis with Participle

| Periphrasis | Meaning | Example |
|---|---|---|
| **tener** + participle | to have (result state) | Tengo hechos los deberes. |
| **llevar** + participle | to have (accumulated) | Llevo leídos tres capítulos. |
| **dejar** + participle | to leave in a state | Dejó la puerta cerrada. |

### Deber vs Deber de
This is an important distinction at B2:
- **Deber + infinitive** = obligation: **Debes** estudiar. (You must study.)
- **Deber de + infinitive** = probability: **Debe de** ser tarde. (It must be late.)

In practice, many speakers confuse them, but in formal writing the distinction matters.

### Llevar + Time + Gerund
This structure has no direct English equivalent and is very useful:
- **Llevo tres años viviendo** aquí. — I've been living here for three years.
- **¿Cuánto tiempo llevas estudiando** español? — How long have you been studying Spanish?
key_points: Verbal periphrasis = conjugated auxiliary + infinitive/gerund/participle
Deber + inf. = obligation; deber de + inf. = probability
Llevar + time + gerund expresses duration: Llevo dos horas esperando
Volver a + inf. = to do again; dejar de + inf. = to stop doing; acabar de + inf. = to have just done
Ponerse a / echarse a + inf. express sudden beginning of an action

vocab_list.example: Suelo desayunar a las ocho.
vocab_list.example_meaning: I usually have breakfast at eight.

vocab_list.example: Dejé de comer carne hace un año.
vocab_list.example_meaning: I stopped eating meat a year ago.

vocab_list.example: Volvió a llamarme por la noche.
vocab_list.example_meaning: He called me again in the evening.

vocab_list.example: Acabo de terminar el libro.
vocab_list.example_meaning: I have just finished the book.

ch_gram_b2_12.title: Passive Se Construction
ch_gram_b2_12.theory:
## Passive Se Construction (La Pasiva con Se / Se Pasivo)

Spanish has multiple ways to express passive meaning. The **passive se** construction is the most common in everyday speech, far more frequent than the traditional passive voice (ser + past participle).

### Formation

**Se + verb (3rd person) + subject**

The verb agrees with the grammatical subject (the thing being acted upon):
- **Se vende** esta casa. — This house is for sale. (singular)
- **Se venden** estas casas. — These houses are for sale. (plural)
- **Se habla** español aquí. — Spanish is spoken here.
- **Se hablan** tres idiomas. — Three languages are spoken.

### Key Uses

1. **General statements (no specific agent)**:
   - En España **se cena** tarde. — In Spain, dinner is eaten late.
   - **Se dice** que va a llover. — It is said that it's going to rain.

2. **Signs and advertisements**:
   - **Se alquila** piso. — Apartment for rent.
   - **Se busca** camarero. — Waiter wanted.
   - **Se necesitan** voluntarios. — Volunteers needed.

3. **Rules, instructions, and processes**:
   - **Se mezclan** los ingredientes. — The ingredients are mixed.
   - Primero **se corta** la cebolla. — First the onion is cut.

### Passive Se vs Impersonal Se

Both use **se** but have different structures:

| Type | Structure | Example |
|---|---|---|
| **Passive se** | Se + verb (agrees with subject) | Se vende**n** coches. (Cars are sold.) |
| **Impersonal se** | Se + verb (3rd person singular only) | Se vive bien aquí. (One lives well here.) |

**Impersonal se** is used when:
- The verb is intransitive: **Se vive** bien. (One lives well.)
- The object is a person (with **a**): **Se entrevistó a** los candidatos. (The candidates were interviewed.)

### Passive Se vs Ser + Past Participle

| Construction | Use | Example |
|---|---|---|
| **Passive se** | Unknown/unimportant agent, everyday speech | Se construyó el puente en 2010. |
| **Ser + participle** | Agent is mentioned, formal/journalistic | El puente fue construido por el gobierno. |

### Common Pitfall
With people as the object, use impersonal se (singular verb + **a**):
- **Se entrevistó a** los candidatos. (NOT ~~Se entrevistaron los candidatos.~~)
- **Se ayudó a** los refugiados. (NOT ~~Se ayudaron los refugiados.~~)
key_points: Passive se: Se + verb (agrees with subject noun) — Se venden coches
Impersonal se: Se + 3rd person singular verb — Se vive bien aquí
With human objects use impersonal se + a: Se entrevistó a los candidatos
Passive se is far more common in speech than ser + past participle
The verb must agree in number with the subject: Se vende (sg.) vs Se venden (pl.)

vocab_list.example_meaning: Apartment for sale in the center.

ch_gram_b2_13.title: Subjunctive in Adjective Clauses
ch_gram_b2_13.theory:
## Subjunctive in Adjective Clauses (Cláusulas Adjetivas / De Relativo)

Adjective clauses (also called relative clauses) describe or modify a noun. The choice between **indicative** and **subjunctive** in these clauses depends on whether the noun being described is **known/existing** or **unknown/non-existent/hypothetical**.

### The Rule

| Antecedent | Mood | Example |
|---|---|---|
| **Known / Existing** | Indicative | Tengo un amigo que **habla** chino. |
| **Unknown / Sought** | Subjunctive | Busco un amigo que **hable** chino. |
| **Non-existent / Denied** | Subjunctive | No hay nadie que **hable** chino aquí. |

### Detailed Examples

**Known antecedent → Indicative:**
- Conozco a un profesor que **enseña** muy bien. — I know a teacher who teaches very well. (I know this specific person.)
- Tenemos un apartamento que **tiene** tres habitaciones. — We have an apartment that has three bedrooms.

**Unknown/sought antecedent → Subjunctive:**
- Necesito un profesor que **enseñe** bien. — I need a teacher who teaches well. (I haven't found one yet.)
- Buscamos un apartamento que **tenga** tres habitaciones. — We're looking for an apartment that has three bedrooms.
- ¿Conoces a alguien que **sepa** programar? — Do you know someone who knows how to code?

**Non-existent antecedent → Subjunctive:**
- No hay ningún restaurante que **sirva** comida mexicana. — There is no restaurant that serves Mexican food.
- No conozco a nadie que **haya estado** en la Antártida. — I don't know anyone who has been to Antarctica.

### Key Triggers for Subjunctive
- **Buscar** (to look for) + unknown: Busco algo que **sea** barato.
- **Necesitar** (to need) + unknown: Necesito alguien que **pueda** ayudarme.
- **Querer** (to want) + unknown: Quiero un coche que **consuma** poco.
- **No hay** / **No existe** + negated: No hay nada que **podamos** hacer.
- **¿Hay...?** / **¿Conoces...?** + uncertain: ¿Hay alguien que **sepa** la respuesta?

### Indicative vs Subjunctive — Meaning Change
- Busco **al** secretario que **habla** inglés. — I'm looking for the secretary who speaks English. (I know who he is; specific person with **al**.)
- Busco **un** secretario que **hable** inglés. — I'm looking for a secretary who speaks English. (Any secretary with that skill; indefinite **un**.)

Notice how the article (**al** vs **un**) and the mood work together to signal specificity.
key_points: Known/existing antecedent → indicative: Tengo un amigo que habla chino
Unknown/sought antecedent → subjunctive: Busco un amigo que hable chino
Non-existent antecedent → subjunctive: No hay nadie que sepa
The definite article (el/la) usually signals indicative; indefinite (un/una) may signal subjunctive
Key trigger verbs: buscar, necesitar, querer + undefined noun

vocab_list.example_meaning: I'm looking for a job that allows me to travel.

ch_gram_b2_14.title: Hypothetical Comparisons
ch_gram_b2_14.theory:
## Hypothetical Comparisons (Comparaciones Hipotéticas)

Hypothetical comparisons express **unreal or imaginary** comparisons. They use structures like **como si**, **cual si**, and **igual que si**, all of which require the **subjunctive**.

### Como si + Subjunctive

The most common structure. **Como si** (as if) is always followed by the past subjunctive or pluperfect subjunctive — never the present subjunctive or indicative.

| Timeframe | Structure | Example |
|---|---|---|
| Same time as main verb | como si + past subjunctive | Habla **como si supiera** todo. |
| Before the main verb | como si + pluperfect subjunctive | Habla **como si hubiera vivido** allí. |

### Detailed Examples

**Como si + past subjunctive (simultaneous/general):**
- Gasta dinero **como si fuera** millonario. — He spends money as if he were a millionaire.
- Me mira **como si no me conociera**. — She looks at me as if she didn't know me.
- Actúan **como si no pasara** nada. — They act as if nothing were happening.

**Como si + pluperfect subjunctive (prior action):**
- Hablaba del tema **como si hubiera estudiado** durante años. — He talked about the topic as if he had studied for years.
- Se comportó **como si no hubiera pasado** nada. — He behaved as if nothing had happened.

### Other Hypothetical Comparison Structures

1. **Igual que si** + subjunctive (same as como si, less common):
   - Lo dijo **igual que si fuera** una broma. — He said it just as if it were a joke.

2. **Como para** + infinitive (as if to / enough to):
   - No es **como para** preocuparse. — It's not something to worry about.
   - Hacía un frío **como para** no salir de casa. — It was cold enough to not leave the house.

3. **Parecer que** / **Parece como si**:
   - **Parece como si fuera** a llover. — It looks as if it's going to rain.
   - **Parece que hubiera** llovido. — It looks like it rained.

### Tense Sequence Summary

| Main Verb Tense | Como si + ... |
|---|---|
| Present | past subjunctive: Habla como si **supiera**. |
| Preterite | past subjunctive or pluperfect subj.: Habló como si **supiera** / **hubiera sabido**. |
| Imperfect | past subjunctive or pluperfect subj.: Hablaba como si **supiera**. |

### Common Pitfall
**Never use the present subjunctive or indicative after como si:**
- ~~como si sabe~~ → como si **supiera**
- ~~como si puede~~ → como si **pudiera**
key_points: Como si always requires past subjunctive or pluperfect subjunctive — never indicative or present subjunctive
Past subjunctive after como si for simultaneous actions; pluperfect for prior actions
Parece como si + subjunctive = 'It looks as if...'
Como para + infinitive expresses 'enough to' or 'as if to'
The tense of the main verb does not change the mood requirement after como si

ch_gram_b2_15.title: Emphatic Constructions
ch_gram_b2_15.theory:
## Emphatic Constructions (Construcciones Enfáticas)

Emphatic constructions allow you to **highlight or stress** a particular element of a sentence. Spanish has several strategies for emphasis that differ from English.

### 1. Cleft Sentences with Ser (Oraciones Hendidas)

These use **ser** to focus attention on one element:

**Es/Fue + focused element + el/la que / quien / donde / cuando...**

- **Fue María la que** me llamó. — It was María who called me.
- **Es aquí donde** vivo. — It is here where I live.
- **Fue ayer cuando** lo vi. — It was yesterday when I saw him.
- **Es a ti a quien** busco. — It is you whom I'm looking for.

### 2. Lo que... es/fue (Pseudo-cleft)

This construction fronts the information for emphasis:

- **Lo que** necesito **es** descansar. — What I need is to rest.
- **Lo que** me molesta **es** su actitud. — What bothers me is his attitude.
- **Lo que** hizo **fue** salir corriendo. — What he did was run out.

### 3. Sí que (emphatic affirmation)

**Sí que** strongly affirms something, often contradicting a previous statement:

- — No estudiaste. — You didn't study.
- — **Sí que** estudié. — I DID study.
- **Sí que** es caro este restaurante. — This restaurant IS expensive.

### 4. Emphatic Pronoun Placement

Placing a pronoun at the beginning or using a prepositional pronoun for emphasis:

- **A mí** me gusta el chocolate. — I like chocolate. (emphasis on "I")
- **A él** no le importa. — He doesn't care. (emphasis on "he")
- Eso lo sé **yo**. — I know that. (emphasis on "I")

### 5. Ser + quien/el que for Agent Emphasis

- **Yo fui quien** lo hizo. / **Yo fui el que** lo hizo. — I was the one who did it.
- **Tú eres la que** siempre llega tarde. — You are the one who always arrives late.

### 6. Reduplication for Emphasis

Repeating words intensifies meaning:
- Está **lejos, lejos**. — It's far, far away.
- Lo hizo **bien, bien**. — He did it really well.

### 7. Pero si... (surprise/emphasis)

Expresses surprise or reinforcement:
- **Pero si** acabo de llegar. — But I just got here!
- **Pero si** eso ya lo sabías. — But you already knew that!
key_points: Cleft sentences: Fue María la que me llamó (It was María who called me)
Lo que... es/fue: Lo que necesito es descansar (What I need is to rest)
Sí que emphasizes affirmation, often contradicting: Sí que estudié (I DID study)
Prepositional pronouns for emphasis: A mí me gusta, A él no le importa
Pero si expresses surprise or reinforcement: Pero si acabo de llegar!

ch_gram_b2_16.title: Sino vs Pero
ch_gram_b2_16.theory:
## Sino vs Pero — When to Use Each

Both **pero** and **sino** translate to "but" in English, but they are used in different contexts and are **not interchangeable**.

### Pero (But — adds contrasting information)

**Pero** introduces information that **contrasts with but does not contradict** the first clause:

- Es caro, **pero** es bueno. — It's expensive, but it's good.
- Estoy cansado, **pero** voy a seguir. — I'm tired, but I'm going to keep going.
- No es grande, **pero** es cómodo. — It's not big, but it's comfortable.

### Sino (But rather — corrects/replaces)

**Sino** is used after a **negative clause** to **correct or replace** the negated information:

- No es rojo, **sino** azul. — It's not red, but (rather) blue.
- No quiero café, **sino** té. — I don't want coffee, but (rather) tea.
- No vive en Madrid, **sino** en Barcelona. — He doesn't live in Madrid, but in Barcelona.

### Sino que (But rather — with conjugated verbs)

When the correction involves a **conjugated verb**, use **sino que**:

- No trabaja, **sino que** estudia. — He doesn't work, but (rather) studies.
- No me llamó, **sino que** me envió un mensaje. — He didn't call me, but sent me a message.
- No salió corriendo, **sino que** se quedó tranquilo. — He didn't run off, but stayed calm.

### No solo... sino (también) — Not only... but (also)

This correlative structure emphasizes addition after negation:

- **No solo** habla español, **sino también** francés. — He not only speaks Spanish but also French.
- **No solo** es inteligente, **sino que también** es amable. — She is not only intelligent but also kind.

### Decision Flowchart

1. Is the first clause negative AND the second clause **corrects/replaces** it?
   - **Yes** → Use **sino** (or **sino que** with a conjugated verb)
   - **No** → Use **pero**

### Tricky Cases

| Sentence | Connector | Why |
|---|---|---|
| No es fácil, **pero** es posible. | pero | Not replacing — adding new info |
| No es fácil, **sino** difícil. | sino | Replacing fácil with difícil |
| No come carne, **pero** come pescado. | pero | Not correcting — adding different info |
| No come carne, **sino** pescado. | sino | Replacing carne with pescado |

### Common Pitfall
- After an affirmative clause, always use **pero**, never **sino**:
  - ~~Es bonito sino caro~~ → Es bonito, **pero** caro.
- **Sino** can only follow a negative clause.
key_points: Pero adds contrasting information: Es caro, pero bueno
Sino corrects/replaces after a negative clause: No es rojo, sino azul
Sino que is used when the replacement involves a conjugated verb
No solo... sino también = not only... but also
Sino can ONLY follow a negative clause; pero can follow any clause

vocab_list.example_meaning: It's not a problem, but rather an opportunity.

vocab_list.example_meaning: He didn't buy it, but rather rented it.

ch_gram_b2_17.title: Subjunctive Tense Agreement
ch_gram_b2_17.theory:
## Subjunctive Tense Agreement (Concordancia Temporal del Subjuntivo)

When a sentence requires the subjunctive in the subordinate clause, the **tense of the main verb** determines which **subjunctive tense** should be used in the dependent clause. This is called the **sequence of tenses** (concordancia temporal).

### The Two Spheres

Spanish divides tenses into two spheres:

| Sphere | Main Verb Tenses | Subjunctive Used |
|---|---|---|
| **Present sphere** | Present, Future, Present Perfect, Imperative | Present subjunctive / Present perfect subjunctive |
| **Past sphere** | Preterite, Imperfect, Conditional, Pluperfect | Past subjunctive / Pluperfect subjunctive |

### Present Sphere Examples

Main verb in present/future → subordinate uses **present subjunctive** or **present perfect subjunctive**:

- **Quiero** que **vengas**. — I want you to come.
- **Espero** que **hayas aprobado**. — I hope you have passed.
- **Le diré** que **traiga** la comida. — I'll tell him to bring the food.
- **Es importante** que **estudies**. — It's important that you study.

### Past Sphere Examples

Main verb in past/conditional → subordinate uses **past subjunctive** or **pluperfect subjunctive**:

- **Quería** que **vinieras**. — I wanted you to come.
- **Le pedí** que **trajera** la comida. — I asked him to bring the food.
- **Dudaba** que **hubieran aprobado**. — I doubted that they had passed.
- **Sería** mejor que **estudiaras**. — It would be better if you studied.
- **Era importante** que **estudiaran**. — It was important that they study.

### Complete Tense Agreement Table

| Main Clause Tense | Simultaneous/Future (subord.) | Prior (subord.) |
|---|---|---|
| Present: Quiero que... | **venga** (pres. subj.) | **haya venido** (pres. perf. subj.) |
| Preterite: Quise que... | **viniera** (past subj.) | **hubiera venido** (pluperf. subj.) |
| Imperfect: Quería que... | **viniera** (past subj.) | **hubiera venido** (pluperf. subj.) |
| Future: Querré que... | **venga** (pres. subj.) | **haya venido** (pres. perf. subj.) |
| Conditional: Querría que... | **viniera** (past subj.) | **hubiera venido** (pluperf. subj.) |

### Flexibility and Exceptions

In some cases, the sequence can be broken for emphasis or when the subordinate action has present relevance:

- **Me pidió** que le **llame** mañana. — He asked me to call him tomorrow. (Past main verb, but present subjunctive because the action is future.)
- **No creo** que **fuera** tan difícil. — I don't think it was that difficult. (Present main verb with past subjunctive referring to past events.)

These "broken" sequences are acceptable and common in real speech.

### Common Pitfall
Students often use the present subjunctive after a past main verb:
- ~~Quería que vengas~~ → Quería que **vinieras**.
- ~~Le pedí que traiga~~ → Le pedí que **trajera**.
key_points: Present sphere (present/future main verb) → present subjunctive: Quiero que vengas
Past sphere (past/conditional main verb) → past subjunctive: Quería que vinieras
For prior actions, use perfect forms: Espero que hayas venido / Dudaba que hubiera venido
Sequence can be broken when the subordinate action has present/future relevance
Common error: using present subjunctive after past main verb (Quería que vengas → vinieras)

ch_gram_b2_18.title: Preposition + Relative Pronoun
ch_gram_b2_18.theory:
## Preposition + Relative Pronoun (Preposición + Pronombre Relativo)

In Spanish, when a relative clause requires a preposition, the preposition must come **before** the relative pronoun — unlike English, where the preposition can go at the end of the sentence.

### English vs Spanish Word Order

| English (informal) | English (formal) | Spanish |
|---|---|---|
| The person I spoke **to** | The person **to** whom I spoke | La persona **con la que** hablé |
| The house I live **in** | The house **in** which I live | La casa **en la que** vivo |
| The reason I came **for** | The reason **for** which I came | La razón **por la que** vine |

### Structures with Prepositions

**Preposition + el/la/los/las que:**
- La empresa **para la que** trabajo es internacional. — The company I work for is international.
- El tema **sobre el que** hablamos es interesante. — The topic we talked about is interesting.
- Las personas **con las que** viajé son mis compañeros. — The people I traveled with are my colleagues.

**Preposition + quien(es)** (people only):
- La persona **con quien** hablé era amable. — The person I spoke with was kind.
- Los amigos **a quienes** invité no vinieron. — The friends I invited didn't come.

**Preposition + el/la cual, los/las cuales** (formal):
- El edificio **en el cual** vivimos es antiguo. — The building in which we live is old.
- La razón **por la cual** dimitió es desconocida. — The reason for which he resigned is unknown.

### Common Preposition + Relative Pronoun Combinations

| Combination | Meaning | Example |
|---|---|---|
| **en el/la que** | in which | La ciudad en la que nací |
| **con el/la que** | with which/whom | El chico con el que salgo |
| **para el/la que** | for which/whom | El trabajo para el que estudié |
| **por el/la que** | for which / through which | La razón por la que vine |
| **del que / de la que** | of/from which | El libro del que te hablé |
| **al que / a la que** | to which | La fiesta a la que fuimos |
| **sin el/la que** | without which | La herramienta sin la que no puedo trabajar |
| **sobre el/la que** | about which | El tema sobre el que escribí |

### Donde, Adonde, Como, Cuando

Relative adverbs can sometimes replace preposition + relative pronoun:

- La ciudad **en la que** nací = La ciudad **donde** nací — The city where I was born.
- El lugar **al que** vamos = El lugar **adonde** vamos — The place where we're going.

### Common Pitfall: Stranded Prepositions
Spanish **never** strands prepositions at the end of a clause (unlike English):
- ~~La persona que hablé con~~ → La persona **con la que** hablé.
- ~~El libro que te hablé de~~ → El libro **del que** te hablé.

### Agreement
The article in **el/la/los/las que** must agree with the antecedent:
- El chico **con el que** salgo (masc. sg.)
- La chica **con la que** salgo (fem. sg.)
- Los amigos **con los que** salgo (masc. pl.)
- Las amigas **con las que** salgo (fem. pl.)
key_points: Prepositions always come BEFORE the relative pronoun in Spanish, never at the end
Preposition + el/la/los/las que is the most common structure
Preposition + quien(es) is used for people only
The article must agree in gender and number with the antecedent
Donde can replace en el/la que for places: La ciudad donde nací
